title: Clip a candy thermometer onto a saucepan's rim, probe hanging clear of the floor, while the other hand holds the pan
instruction: Holding the saucepan by its handle, clip the candy thermometer onto its rim so it hangs inside, dial up, tip clear of the floor.
context: Restaurant and pastry cooks clip a candy or deep-fry thermometer to the pan before they cook sugar syrup, caramel, custard or frying oil, and leave it there to read the temperature hands-free. O*NET 35-2014.00 Cooks, Restaurant, core task: "Ensure food is stored and cooked at correct temperature"; about 1.4 million US restaurant cooks (BLS OEWS 35-2014). The thermometer must go from lying on the counter to hanging stem-down and in over the rim, and its spring clip must be pushed down over the rim, one leg inside the pan and one outside, until its bend sits on the rim. The clip holds the stem only by friction: pushed too hard, the stem slides down through it and the tip rests on the hot floor, where it reads the metal instead of the food. The other hand holds the light pan by its handle.
setup: Millimetres from the midpoint between the arm bases: x forward, y to the robot's left, heights above the bench. 1) Saucepan: a Vollrath 682115 Wear-Ever 1.5 qt tapered aluminium sauce pan (maker's figures: 158.0 across the rim, 152.9 inside, base 142.1, 92.1 deep inside, 334.3 long with its handle, 107 high to the handle's top, 11 gauge aluminium, double-thick rim, black silicone handle), empty and cold, standing on the bench with its base centred at (120, 60) and its handle pointing straight to the robot's right (-y); mark the base's outline on the bench with tape. Estimates: wall 2.55 (from the two diameters), bottom 4.6, handle 24 wide x 16 thick, 0.55 kg (check: ruler, kitchen scale). 2) Thermometer: a Taylor 3505 TruTemp candy/deep-fry dial thermometer (2 in dial, 6 in stainless stem, stainless pan clip that slides on the stem). Before each trial slide the clip along the stem until the underside of its top bend is 72 mm from the tip (ruler): seated on this pan's rim the tip then hangs about 20 mm off the floor. It lies on the bench to the left of the pan: tip at (45, 200), stem along +x, so the dial's middle is near (204, 200) with its face toward +x; the clip hangs straight down under the stem, the thermometer resting on the dial's rim and the clip's lower end. Estimates (ruler, kitchen scale): stem 4.8 across, dial case 13 deep (14 with the lens), thermometer 40 g without its clip, 46 g with it; clip 12 wide, its top bend 14 out from the stem, inner leg 16 long plus a 5 lead-in, outer leg 14 long plus an 8 flare, legs 4.5 apart under the bend closing to 2.2 at the outer leg's end; the clip grips the rim with about 1 N; the stem slides through the clip's sleeve only past about 20 N (hang a 2 kg weight from the dial while holding the clip: it should just start to slide). Frictions (estimates): stainless 0.35, aluminium 0.40. Start: both arms at their ready pose, grippers open. The README lists every collider and joint.
scoring: Judged at the end of the trial from the top-camera video, a side photo and a ruler (in simulation from the poses). Hooked: the pan's rim is between the clip's two legs (one leg inside the pan, one outside) and the clip's top bend is no more than 16 mm above the rim. Bend height: from the rim's top to the underside of the clip's top bend, ruler, side photo. Tip gap: the tip's height above the inside floor, read as 92 mm + bend height - (152 mm - L), where L is the stem's length from the dial's back to the clip's top bend (ruler); a tip that touches the floor is seen directly. Pan shift: the base's largest offset from its tape outline. Tilt: the stem's angle from vertical (phone level on the dial's face). Score 0 if: the thermometer is not hooked on the rim, or a gripper still touches it (any gripper within 3 cm of it), or its tip is outside the pan or within 1 mm of the floor (touching), or the pan moved more than 30 mm, tipped more than 20 degrees, or anything left the bench. Doing nothing scores 0. Otherwise the score is the lowest of: bend height (1.0 up to 3 mm; 0.5 over 3 to 10 mm; 0.25 over 10 mm); tip gap (1.0 from 10 mm; 0.5 from 5 to under 10 mm; 0.25 from 1 to under 5 mm); pan shift (1.0 up to 10 mm; 0.75 over 10 to 20 mm; 0.5 over 20 to 30 mm); tilt (1.0 up to 10 degrees; 0.5 over 10 to 20; 0.25 over 20). A trial whose thermometer is still moving (more than 1 mm or 2 degrees in its last second) scores at most 0.75.
reset_notes: About 1 minute. Unclip the thermometer by lifting it straight up off the rim. Check with a ruler that the clip's top bend is still 72 mm from the tip; slide it back if the stem slipped. Lay the thermometer back at its start place (tip at the mark at (45, 200), stem along +x, clip hanging down under the stem). Set the pan back in its tape outline with its handle pointing to the robot's right. The pan stays empty and cold; nothing is heated. Return both arms to the ready pose.
fidelity: Rigid bodies. The clip's spring is its outer leg on a hinge with a preloaded spring (about 1 N on the rim); its sleeve's grip on the stem is a slide that moves only past about 20 N (16 N moving); the clip cannot turn on the stem. The pan's wall is 64 convex pieces at the maker's sizes; the stem's tip is flat. Empty, cold pan: no liquid or heat. Clip shape, spring, grip, masses and frictions are estimates.
